{"returncode":0,"stdout":"// include/strata/core/layout.hpp - the pack's LAYOUT, resolved by name and checked against the kernels.\n//\n// `WeightTable` answers \"where are the bytes\".  This answers \"is this the tensor I think it is\", and it is\n// the layer where a pack and a kernel disagree - which is the failure this project keeps paying for. A mismatch is reported with the tensor name, the shape found and the shape required,\n// at LOAD time - not as a wrong number inside a GEMV at token 4000.\n#pragma once\n\n#include \"strata/core/weights.hpp\"\n\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <string>\n\nnamespace strata::core {\n\n/// The model's geometry, taken from `docs/semantics.md` and the artifact's own metadata.  Every field here\n/// is a number a kernel depends on, so a change is a change to a kernel contract and not a tuning knob.\nstruct ModelGeometry {\n    int64_t n_embd = 2560;\n    int64_t n_layers = 48;\n    int64_t qsa_interval = 4;      ///< every 4th layer is full attention: layers 3, 7, ... 47\n\n    // GDN (36 layers)\n    int64_t ssm_state_size = 128;\n    int64_t ssm_k_heads = 16;\n    int64_t ssm_v_heads = 48;\n    int64_t ssm_d_conv = 4;\n    int64_t ssm_conv_channels = 10240;   ///< 2*128*16 + 128*48\n    int64_t ssm_value_dim = 6144;        ///< 128 * 48\n\n    // QSA (12 layers)\n    int64_t n_head = 24;\n    int64_t n_head_kv = 2;\n    int64_t head_dim = 256;\n    int64_t idx_q_heads = 4;\n    int64_t idx_key_dim = 128;\n\n    // gated residual, on every layer\n    int64_t hc = 4;\n    int64_t hc_lr = 320;\n\n    // MoE, on every layer\n    int64_t n_expert = 512;\n    int64_t n_ff = 640;\n\n    int64_t hc_dim() const { return hc * n_embd; }\n    /// `layer % qsa_interval == qsa_interval - 1` is full attention.  Derived, not a second list.\n    int64_t n_qsa_layers() const { return n_layers / qsa_interval; }\n    int64_t n_gdn_layers() const { return n_layers - n_qsa_layers(); }\n};\n\n/// True for the full-attention layers.  `docs/semantics.md` gives this twice over - `full_attention_interval\n/// = 4` and an explicit `attention.compress_ratios` array - and this is the first of the two.\ninline bool is_qsa_layer(const ModelGeometry& g, int64_t layer) {\n    return layer % g.qsa_interval == g.qsa_interval - 1;\n}\n\n/// One layer's tensors, resolved by NAME.  `get(\"attn_qkv.weight\")` looks up `blk.<layer>.attn_qkv.weight`\n/// and returns null if the pack does not have it - a null is information, because a GDN layer has no\n/// `attn_q` and a QSA layer has no `attn_qkv`.\n///\n/// Holds a reference to the table; the table must outlive it.\nclass LayerView {\npublic:\n    LayerView(const WeightTable& table, int64_t layer) : table_(&table), layer_(layer) {}\n\n    int64_t layer() const { return layer_; }\n    std::string name(const char* suffix) const;\n    const WeightRef* get(const char* suffix) const { return table_->find(name(suffix)); }\n\nprivate:\n","stderr":""}

{"returncode":0,"stdout":"// include/strata/core/hit_hook.hpp - R4.2c: the seam between the host loop and the VRAM expert tier.\n//\n// **IT IS ITS OWN HEADER BECAUSE BOTH SIDES NEED IT AND NEITHER SHOULD OWN IT.**  `session.hpp` declares the\n// loop that calls the hook; `expert_source.hpp` declares the implementation that answers it.  Putting the type\n// in either one makes the other include a header it has no other use for, and the loop knowing what an expert\n// cache is (or the adapter knowing what a graph is) is exactly the coupling this seam exists to avoid.\n#pragma once\n\n#include <cstdint>\n\nnamespace strata::core {\n\n/// **TWO PHASES, AND THE SPLIT IS THE WHOLE POINT.**  `Launch` runs BEFORE the CPU pool and `Combine` runs\n/// AFTER the misses have been copied into `parts`.  That ordering is what lets the GPU's resident experts run\n/// at the same time as the CPU's misses instead of after them:\n///\n///     ring -> hits(Launch)   [GPU: quantize + grouped experts into `hit_out`]\n///          -> pool()         [CPU: the misses, CONCURRENT with the GPU]\n///          -> H2D misses into `parts`\n///          -> hits(Combine)  [GPU: parts += hit_out]\n///          -> post[l]\n///\n/// **MEASURED, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ORDER.**  The first version called the hit path once, after the\n/// pool, writing straight into `parts`.  The drain duly fell **18.2 -> 10.2 ms** - the CPU really was doing\n/// half the experts - and **the token did not move at all**, because the GPU's half had simply been moved onto\n/// the critical path behind the CPU's instead of beside it.  A second buffer and one `add_inplace` buy the\n/// overlap back.\nenum class HitPhase { Launch, Combine };\n\n/// `ids` AND `k` ARE THE ROUTER'S OWN OUTPUT, AND THEY ARE WHY THIS HOOK TAKES ARGUMENTS AT ALL.\n///\n/// The first version took only `(user, stream, phase)` and left the hit/miss decision inside the pool\n/// callback - which runs AFTER `Launch`.  So `Launch` read the hit list from the PREVIOUS layer and computed\n/// the previous layer's experts into the current layer's rows.  It produced a token, the timings looked\n/// plausible, and **C1 moved from mean KL 9.69e-02 to 1.03e+00 and top-1 from 0.867 to 0.333.**  The decision\n/// has to happen in `Launch`, on the ids the doorbell published for THIS layer, and the pool then consumes it.\n///\n/// A null `HitFn` means \"no VRAM tier\" - the default, and what every caller had before R4.\nusing HitFn = void (*)(void* user, void* stream, HitPhase phase, const int32_t* ids, int64_t k);\n\n}  // namespace strata::core\n","stderr":""}

### ExpertCache::admit (global and per-layer)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**Global admission** (per\_layer = false):

$$\text{admit}(l, e) = \begin{cases}
-1 & \text{if } \text{next\_free} \ge S \\
\text{next\_free} & \text{otherwise};\quad \text{residency}[l \cdot N_E + e] \leftarrow \text{next\_free},\; \text{next\_free} \mathrel{+}= 1
\end{cases}$$

**Per-layer admission** (per\_layer = true), $q = \lfloor S / N_L \rfloor$:

$$\text{layer\_range}(l) = \begin{cases}
[l \cdot q,\; (l+1) \cdot q) & l < N_L - 1 \\
[l \cdot q,\; S) & l = N_L - 1
\end{cases}$$

$$\text{admit}(l, e) = \begin{cases}
-1 & \text{if } \text{layer\_next}[l] \ge \text{hi}(l) \\
\text{layer\_next}[l] & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}$$

**Invariant:** no eviction. Once $\text{residency}[i] \neq -1$, it is never changed.

```lean
    let q := S / N_L
    (l1 * q + q ≤ l2 * q) ∨ (l2 * q + q ≤ l1 * q) ∨ l1 = N_L - 1 ∨ l2 = N_L - 1 := by sorry
```

### gdn_step

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

State layout: $(S, h_v, S)$ — transposed from reference $(S, S, h_v)$ for coalescing.

Head pairing: head $h$ of value uses key head $h \bmod h_k$ (MODULO, not interleave).

For each column $(i_0, h, j)$ independently:
$$\text{dec}_h = \exp(\text{gate}_h)$$
$$\text{st}[i, h, j] \mathrel{*}= \text{dec}_h \quad \forall i$$
$$\text{sk}_{h,j} = \sum_i \text{st}[i, h, j] \cdot k[h \bmod h_k, i]$$
$$d_{h,j} = (v[h,j] - \text{sk}_{h,j}) \cdot \beta_h$$
$$\text{st}[i, h, j] \mathrel{+}= k[h \bmod h_k, i] \cdot d_{h,j} \quad \forall i$$
$$o[h,j] = \sum_i \text{st}[i, h, j] \cdot q[h \bmod h_k, i]$$

**Critical ordering:** decay BEFORE rank-1 update (Property 5 of reference).

**Preconditions:** $q, k$ are L2-normalized; $q$ is pre-scaled by $1/\sqrt{S}$; $\beta$ is post-sigmoid.

#### LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)

```lean

    h % h_k < h_k := by sorry

-- axle_verify: content

    h % h_k < h_k := by
  omega
```

### gdn_conv_step

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$\text{inp} = [\text{conv\_state} \mid x] \in \mathbb{R}^{d_\text{conv} \times C}$$

$$\text{out}[c] = \sum_{i=0}^{d_\text{conv}-1} \text{inp}[i, c] \cdot kW[c \cdot d_\text{conv} + i]$$

Post: oldest row of conv\_state is discarded, $x$ is shifted in as newest row.

### gdn_l2_norm

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$\text{l2\_norm}(x)_i = \frac{x_i}{\sqrt{\sum_j x_j^2 + \varepsilon}}$$

**Not** $\sqrt{\text{mean}(x^2) + \varepsilon}$. The $\varepsilon$ floors the squared norm, not the mean. Difference is $\sqrt{S} = 11.3\times$.

Applied to $q$ and $k$ rows only ($h_k$ heads each of $S$ elements). **$v$ is NOT normalized.**

### ngram_mixed / ngram_rows

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$\text{ngram\_mixed}(\text{ctx}, \text{mult}, n) = \bigoplus_{i=0}^{n-1} \left(\text{ctx}[i] \cdot \text{mult}[i]\right) \quad (\oplus = \text{XOR},\; \text{uint64})$$

For each token $t$ with predecessors $p_0$ (oldest), $p_1$:
- Context window: $\text{ctx} = [p_0, p_1, t]$, but EOS at position $i$ zeroes positions $\le i$.
- Missing predecessor ($< 0$) contributes 0.

For head $h \in [0, 16)$:
- bigram heads ($h < 8$): use 2-prefix of context
- trigram heads ($h \ge 8$): use full 3-prefix

$$\text{row}[h] = \text{offset}[h] + (\text{ngram\_mixed}(\text{ctx}_h, \text{mult}_h, n_h) \;\%\; \text{vocab}[h])$$

**Critical:** `%` (modulus), NOT `&` (mask) — vocab sizes are NOT powers of two.

### IQ4_NL dequantization

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Codebook $C = \{-127, -104, -83, -65, -49, -35, -22, -10, 1, 13, 25, 38, 53, 69, 89, 113\}$, $|C| = 16$.

No $-8$ subtraction (version-dependent). No offset term (IQ4\_NL has `has_offset = false`).

**Split-half nibble order** (NOT interleaved):
$$y[j] = d \cdot C[\text{qs}[j] \;\&\; \text{0xF}], \quad y[j + 16] = d \cdot C[\text{qs}[j] \gg 4]$$

So byte $j$ carries elements $j$ and $j+16$, not $2j$ and $2j+1$.

One row: 90 bytes → 160 floats. Value $= C[\text{code}] \times \text{scale}$.

#### LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)

### PleTable

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$\text{open}: \text{gguf\_path} \to \mathbb{B}$$
$$\text{gather}(\text{rows}_{16}) \to \text{out}_{2560}: \quad \text{out}[h \cdot 160 \ldots (h+1) \cdot 160) = \text{dequant}(\text{table}[\text{rows}[h]])$$

Head-slowest flatten: row $h$'s 160 values occupy $[h \cdot 160, (h+1) \cdot 160)$.

I/O modes: Direct (unbuffered 4 KiB SSD reads, no mmap during read) or Mmap (OS page-faulted).

GGUF offset: tensor data starts at `shard2_tensor.offset + 192` (header), NOT at file offset 0.

## MODULE: cpu_expert_kernel (AVX512-VNNI Q2_0 expert evaluation)

### Constants & Geometry

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$H = 2560,\; \text{FF} = 640,\; N_E = 512,\; QK = 64,\; QK_A = 32$$
$$BB = 18 \text{ (bytes per 64-weight Q2\_0 block: 2 fp16 scales + 16 code bytes)}$$
$$\text{BLOB} = 3 \times \frac{H \times \text{FF} \times BB}{QK} = 1{,}382{,}400 \text{ bytes per expert}$$

Blob layout offsets:
$$O_{\text{GU\_CODES}} = 0, \quad O_{\text{D\_CODES}} = 2 \cdot \text{FF} \cdot \frac{H}{4}$$
$$O_{\text{GU\_SCALES}} = O_{\text{D\_CODES}} + H \cdot \frac{\text{FF}}{4}$$
$$O_{\text{D\_SCALES}} = O_{\text{GU\_SCALES}} + 2 \cdot \text{FF} \cdot \frac{H}{QK} \cdot 2$$

### ActQ (activation quantization)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Activation quantization into $QK_A = 32$ element chunks:

$$q_i = \text{round}(x_i / \text{scale}_k), \quad \text{scale}_k = \max_{j \in \text{chunk}_k} |x_j| / 127$$
$$\text{sum}_k = \sum_{j \in \text{chunk}_k} q_j$$
$$hx_k = \text{scale}_k \cdot \text{sum}_k$$

**Critical contract:** one weight block ($QK = 64$) spans TWO activation chunks ($QK_A = 32$) with two different scales. Using one scale per weight block is the "natural-looking mistake."

#### LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE

```cpp
struct adjActQ {
    alignas(64) int8_t qvals[ADJ_EMBD];
    float scalevec[ADJ_MAXC];
    int32_t sumvec[ADJ_MAXC];
    float hxvec[ADJ_MAXC];
    int chunkcount;
};
struct adjExpertScratch {
    adjActQ a1;
    adjActQ a2;
    alignas(64) float ffvec[ADJ_FF];
};
```

---

### s2_expert_vnni / s2_expert_vnni_q

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$\text{expert}(x) = \text{down}(\text{swiglu}(\text{gate}(x), \text{up}(x)))$$
$$\text{swiglu}(g, u) = \text{SiLU}(g) \odot u, \quad \text{SiLU}(g) = g \cdot \sigma(g)$$

All three projections are Q2\_0 with the blob layout. The `_q` variant takes pre-quantized activation, avoiding 10x redundant quantization per layer.

**Key x86 instructions:**
- `vpdpbusd` (AVX512-VNNI): 4 int8 MACs per instruction
- `vpmultishiftqb` (AVX512-VBMI): 2-bit code unpacking (argument order: control, data — Intel guide is wrong)
- Float accumulator reduced ONCE at row end (not per 64-weight block)

#### LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)

```lean
-- axle_verify: content

```

### Row-range and multi-token variants

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**Row-range split:** `gu_rows` computes $\text{ff}[r] = \text{SiLU}(\text{gate}_r \cdot x) \times (\text{up}_r \cdot x)$ for $r \in [r_0, r_1)$ of FF. `down_rows` computes $\text{out}[r]$ for $r \in [r_0, r_1)$ of H. Together with intermediate requantization they are bitwise equivalent to the single-call kernel.

**Multi-token:** up to $\text{MAXT} = 8$ tokens routed to the same expert. Blob read and 2-bit unpack done ONCE; VNNI dot per token. Each token's result is bitwise equal to single-token.

### moe_hit_grouped_scratch_bytes

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$\text{scratch\_bytes}(n_h, H, \text{FF}) = n_h \cdot 2 \cdot \text{FF} \cdot 4 \;+\; n_h \cdot \lceil\text{FF}/32\rceil \cdot 34$$

Two regions: gate/up activations ($n_h \times 2 \times \text{FF}$ floats) and quantized intermediate ($n_h \times (\text{FF}/32) \times 34$ bytes).

Carved from caller's arena (no cudaMalloc allowed on token path or during stream capture).

### moe_hit_grouped_s2

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

For each hit $h \in [0, n_h)$:
1. **Gate/Up GEMV:** $\text{gu}[h, 2r] = \text{gate}_r \cdot x$, $\text{gu}[h, 2r+1] = \text{up}_r \cdot x$ for $r \in [0, \text{FF})$
2. **SwiGLU:** $\text{ff}[h, r] = \text{SiLU}(\text{gu}[h, 2r]) \cdot \text{gu}[h, 2r+1]$
3. **Requantize:** $\text{ff}_q[h] = \text{quantize\_q8\_0}(\text{ff}[h])$
4. **Down GEMV:** $\text{out}[\text{dst}[h] \cdot H \ldots] = \text{down}(\text{ff}_q[h])$

Expert blob at: $\text{blob\_base} + \text{slot}[h] \cdot \text{blob\_bytes}$

Output destination: $\text{out} + \text{dst}[h] \cdot H$ (router's row index, not sequential).

**`dst_index` purpose:** CPU writes misses at routed indices; GPU writes hits at their routed indices via `dst_index`. `moe_combine` sees a contiguous $(k, H)$ buffer regardless of which engine produced which row.

**`x_scales` (R4.2h):** When non-null, fp32 scales replace fp16 `d` from `block_q8_0`. This closes the fp16-rounding gap ($\max \text{rel} = 4.761 \times 10^{-4}$) between CPU and GPU paths, ensuring a cache hit and miss produce the same number.

**Blob layout:** same as `cpu/expert.hpp`. Gate/up codes interleaved by row, scales are fp16 (differs from dense S-form which uses fp32 scales).

**Four kernel launches per layer**, not five per expert.

#### LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)

```lean

    dst * H + H ≤ k * H := by sorry

-- axle_verify: content
theorem dst_index_in_range (dst k H : Nat) (h : dst < k) :
    dst * H + H ≤ k * H := by
  omega
```

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**moe\_hit\_select:** Given routed ids $[0, k)$ and residency row $\text{res}[e] \in \{-1\} \cup \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$:
$$\forall i \in [0, k):\; \text{if } \text{res}[\text{ids}[i]] \neq -1 \Rightarrow \text{slot}[\text{count}] = \text{res}[\text{ids}[i]],\; \text{dst}[\text{count}] = i,\; \text{count} \mathrel{+}= 1$$

### GdnBuffers

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Buffer set for one GDN layer, all device memory:

| Buffer | Shape | Format | Purpose |
|--------|-------|--------|---------|
| $x_{q8k}$ | $N_E$ | block\_q8\_K | K-quant activation image |
| $x_{q8\_0}$ | $N_E$ | block\_q8\_0 | Q2/Q4/Q5/Q8 activation image |
| $x_{bf16}$ | $N_E$ | bf16 | BF16 activation image |
| $\text{qkv}$ | $C = 10240$ | f32 | Combined projection output |
| $\text{conv\_out}$ | $C$ | f32 | Conv result |
| $h$ | $C$ | f32 | SiLU(conv\_out), then $q \mid k \mid v$ in-place |
| $\alpha, \beta, \text{gate}$ | $h_v$ | f32 | Per-head scalars |
| $o$ | $h_v \times S$ | f32 | Recurrence output |
| $\text{state}$ | $S \times h_v \times S$ | f32 | Recurrent state (persistent) |
| $\text{conv\_state}$ | $C \times (d_\text{conv} - 1)$ | f32 | Conv history (persistent) |

**Critical ordering from `ref/gdn.py`:**
1. qkv = wqkv @ x
2. conv → **SiLU on WHOLE conv output BEFORE split**
3. q, k = l2\_norm (**v is NOT normalized**)
4. beta = sigmoid(wbeta @ x)
5. gate = softplus(walpha @ x + dt) × ssm\_a
6. recurrent step
7. y = rms\_norm(o, ssm\_norm) × **sigmoid**(z) (not SiLU)
8. out = ssm\_out @ y

**Three activation formats:** attn\_qkv is K-quants (Q8\_K), ssm\_alpha/beta are BF16, and mixing them costs 0.66–1.41% error.

### MoEBuffers and moe_layer

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

MoE block: router → (caller fills `parts`) → combine.

$$\text{logits} = W_\text{router}^{bf16} \cdot x^{bf16}$$
$$\text{ids}, \text{weights} = \text{top-}k(\text{logits})$$
$$\text{out} = \sum_{j=0}^{k-1} \text{weights}[j] \cdot \text{parts}[j] + \text{shared\_expert}(x)$$

**Two critical activation formats:**
1. Router: BF16 activation (measured $8.1 \times 10^{-3}$ error without it — enough to flip top-10 selection)
2. Shared expert: takes fp16 (known gap: should be Q8\_K per contract)

`parts` is filled by the CALLER (CPU pool + VRAM tier). The function owns the two ends (which experts, how combined), deliberately not the middle.

### moe_route / moe_finish / moe_shared / moe_combine_parts

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**Split rationale:** The one-layer delay was NOT a timing change — passing layer $l$'s pool result to layer $l+1$ computes:
$$\sum_j w_{l+1}[j] \cdot \text{expert}_{ids_l, j}(x_l)$$
instead of the correct:
$$\sum_j w_l[j] \cdot \text{expert}_{ids_l, j}(x_l)$$

Both expert selection AND input are one layer stale while weights are current.

**Fix:** split the graph:
- `pre[l]`: attn → mixer → gr\_write → gr\_read → moe\_route [rings doorbell]
- (host runs CPU pool)
- `post[l]`: moe\_finish → gr\_write

`post[l]` launched AFTER pool returns → layer $l$'s experts with layer $l$'s weights.

**`moe_shared` + `moe_combine_parts`:** Decomposition of `moe_finish`. With `shared_early`, shared expert runs in `pre[l]` after doorbell (GPU computes while CPU runs pool).

### QsaState (QSA layer persistent state)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

KV cache in paged layout:
$$K_{\text{pool}}: [\text{page}][n_{kv}][\text{page\_size}][d_h] \in \text{fp16}$$
$$V_{\text{pool}}: \text{same shape}$$

Optional INT8 mode (P7): codes + fp16 scale per 64 values (half VRAM of fp16).

Indexer state: pooled keys, raw tail, dead slot, block positions.

RoPE tables: $(\text{max\_cells}, n_\text{rot}/2)$ floats, built on host in float64.

**Per-token device counts** (captured as graph nodes):
- `step`: counts that every kernel needs
- `pos_dev`: $(n_\text{head},)$ int32, all equal to current position — device memory because RoPE reads positions from device

**Pinned host staging** at FIXED ADDRESSES (not optimisation — CUDA graph captures SOURCE POINTER; stack/vector addresses are dead on replay).

### QsaBuffers and qsa_layer

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Op order from `ref/model.py::_qsa`:
1. Indexer raw key appended BEFORE any norm or rotation

### Doorbell (GPU-to-CPU handoff)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Mapped pinned memory with device and host views of the same bytes:

$$\text{Doorbell} = \{x_f \in \mathbb{R}^{N_E},\; \text{ids} \in \mathbb{Z}^k,\; \text{weights} \in \mathbb{R}^k,\; \text{seq} \in \mathbb{Z}_{32},\; \text{flag} \in \mathbb{Z}_{32}\}$$

**Protocol:**
1. Device writes $x_f$, ids, weights, increments seq (doorbell kernel, capturable)
2. Host polls: reads `h_seq` AND calls `cudaEventQuery` (both required — memory-only spin never runs kernel on WDDM)
3. Host runs pool, writes `h_flag` = ring value
4. Device's `doorbell_wait` spins until flag equals ring

**Why a kernel, not an event:** `cudaEventRecord` inside capture is SILENTLY DROPPED (measured: 2 nodes for two kernels + event, event never completed across 41 ms graph). A kernel is captured normally.

**Measured latency:** host sees pinned handoff 0.050 ms into a 39.8 ms graph.

### BlockBuffers and block_layer

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

The gated-residual stack: $R \in \mathbb{R}^{hc \times N_E}$ — both input and output.

Per-layer op order (§6.1):
$$\text{gr\_read}(\text{attn}) \to \text{mixer} \to \text{gr\_write}(\text{attn})$$

### embed_row / lm_head

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**embed\_row:** Column dequant, not GEMV.

$$\text{out}[i] = W_\text{embd}[i][\text{token}], \quad i \in [0, N_E)$$

Decode must be bit-identical to `s_gemv_q8k_split`: code at bit $(i \bmod \text{PER\_BYTE}) \times \text{CODE\_BITS}$ of byte $i / \text{PER\_BYTE}$; value = $(c + c_\text{bias}) \times \text{scales}[i/g] + \text{offsets}[i/g]$.

**lm\_head:** 
$$\text{fin} = \text{gr\_read}(R, \text{output\_hc\_*}, \text{inject}=\text{None}, \text{rms\_eps})$$
$$\text{logits} = W_\text{output} \cdot \text{fin}$$

### session_token / session_capture / session_replay

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**session\_token:** Layers 0..47 sequentially, each a `block_layer`. $R$ updated in place. `parts` $(k, N_E)$ filled by caller.

**session\_capture:** One graph per layer (bakes in pointers). Per-token data (position, step counts) arrives through fixed-address device buffers. Host decides when each layer runs → CPU pool can start while GPU works.

**Measured speedup:** 1.585 ms vs 2.393 ms (1.51×) — pure launch overhead eliminated.

**session\_replay:** Same arithmetic as `session_token`, ~2000 kernel launches become 48 graph launches.

**session\_replay\_full:** TRUE per-token GPU floor. `session_replay` only launches `pre` graphs (omits 48 `post` graphs). The "39.8 ms pure GPU" figure came from `session_replay` while being described as the whole GPU.

### SessionGraphs

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Per layer: `execs[l]` = pre graph, `posts[l]` = post graph.

Split captures: `preA[l]` (mixer half), `preB[l]` (FFN front + router), `preP[1..5][l]` (prefix graphs for per-stage timing).

**Diagnostic counters:**
- `rings_mid_graph`: layers where ring observed while graph still running (overlap window)
- `ms_to_ring`: cumulative ms from launch to ring observation
- `ms_host`: cumulative ms from ring to next `pre[l+1]` launch (GPU idle window)

**Round trip = `ms_to_ring` + `ms_host`**, measured 0.258 ms/layer with no pool.

### session_loop (host loop with doorbell protocol)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Per-layer protocol:
$$\text{launch } G[l] \to \text{poll doorbell} \to \text{read miss list} \to \text{dispatch pool} \to \text{wait} \to \text{write } y_\text{miss} \to \text{launch } G[l+1]$$

**No `cudaStreamSynchronize` in the loop** (P2.X3). Waiting is `cudaEventQuery` on event recorded after launch.

**Overlap window:** layer publishes $x_f$ at ~71% of its own duration; pool has remaining 29%.

**`dump_layers`:** $(N_L + 1) \times hc \times N_E$ floats. Slot 0 = initial residual, slot $l+1$ = $R$ after layer $l$. D2H copies enqueued as graph nodes, no extra sync.

**SessionLoopScratch:** pinned host staging, probe event, CPU affinity pin. Allocated ONCE at setup (was per-token allocation before — `cudaFreeHost` implicitly syncs device).

### TokenGraph (whole-token graph, P3)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

All 48 layers in one graph. Between `pre[l]` (doorbell ring, shared expert) and parts copy, a one-thread kernel waits ON DEVICE until host writes ring value into `db.h_flag`.

Per layer:
$$\text{pre}[l] \to \text{doorbell\_wait} \to \text{parts} \leftarrow y_\text{miss} \;(\text{H2D}) \to \text{post}[l]$$

Same kernels, same order → bitwise same token. Host only polls rings, runs pool, writes flags — no driver call in loop.

**Measured handoff cost:** 5.2 µs per handoff.

**Under WDDM:** every graph launch costs ~0.3–0.4 ms submission latency × 96 per token = major overhead. Token graph eliminates 95 of 96 launches.

### Stage timing (session_replay_stages variants)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Event pairs around pieces of `block_layer_pre`/`_post`, recorded per (layer, stage). Read once at end — no synchronization during run. Only for `--no-capture` path (events inside stream capture are silently dropped).

**Prefix-graph method (R0.11):** Five prefix graphs per layer, consecutive differences give per-stage times. Residual saved and restored between prefixes (stage 2 = `gr_write` mutates $R$ in place).

**Sweep method (R3.5c):** One prefix type per sweep, all 48 layers back to back. Eliminates bias from switching between different-sized graphs.

{"returncode":0,"stdout":"168\n---\n// include/strata/plan/plan.hpp - P1.S9 census + memory planner.\n//\n// This is the component that makes one binary adapt to the GPU it is running on.  The engine has 33.97 GB of\n// expert weights (has to live in DRAM and be streamed) and a fixed VRAM budget that has to hold the dense\n// weights, the KV cache, the indexer keys, the recurrent state and as many expert-cache slots as remain.\n// Every one of those competes, so the plan is an arithmetic result rather than a configuration choice, and\n// it must REFUSE rather than silently overcommit.\n//\n// DERIVATION POLICY.  `phases/00-README.md` §2 gives three rows of expected values but no formula, so the\n// arithmetic here is derived from the model's geometry and the table is used as a CHECK.  Where the two\n// disagree the geometry wins and the disagreement is reported - a table transcribed by hand is not a\n// specification, and fitting formulas to it would hide exactly the errors this is supposed to catch.\n#pragma once\n\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <stdexcept>\n#include <string>\n#include <vector>\n\nnamespace strata::plan {\n\n// ---- model geometry (the real Qwen3.8-Flash-Next artifact) ------------------\nstruct Geometry {\n    int n_layers = 48;\n    int n_qsa_layers = 12; // layers 3, 7, ... 47 - the full-attention ones\n    int n_kv_heads = 2;\n    int head_dim = 256;\n    int kv_group = 64; // INT8 KV is grouped-64: one fp16 scale per 64 elements\n    int qsa_block = 4; // the indexer pools one key per 4-token block\n    /// THE INDEXER'S KEY STORE, and the trap that has now been walked into twice in opposite directions.\n    ///\n    /// `indexer.q_proj.weight` is [2560, 512] = **4 QUERY heads** of 128.  `indexer.k_proj.weight` is\n    /// [2560, 128] = **ONE shared KEY head**.  The queries are not cached; only the key is.  So the cache\n    /// holds one 128-wide key per TOKEN, pooled to one per `qsa_block`-token block - which\n    /// `include/strata/kernels/qsa.hpp` states directly: `pooled (max_cells/idx_block + 1, idx_dim)`, and\n    /// its own note that the fp32 store is \"50 MiB at 32K\" (12 layers x 8192 blocks x 128 x 4 B = 48 MiB).\n    ///\n    ///   original      indexer_heads(1) * head_dim(256) / 4  = 64 B/token/layer   2x too big\n    ///   round 194     indexer_heads(4) * key_dim(128) / 4   = 128 B/token/layer  4x too big\n    ///   correct       key_heads(1)     * key_dim(128) / 4   =  32 B/token/layer\n    ///\n    /// Round 194 \"fixed\" this by reading `indexer.head_count = 4` out of the metadata and multiplying by it -\n    /// right about the metadata, wrong about what was being counted.  **A head count in the metadata does not\n    /// say WHICH tensor it counts.**\n    int indexer_q_heads = 4;    // query heads: they multiply the SCORES, and cost no cache at all\n    int indexer_key_heads = 1;  // k_proj is [n_embd, 128]: ONE shared key head\n    int indexer_key_dim = 128;  // the key width, and the width of the thing that IS cached\n\n    /// GDN geometry.  `docs/semantics.md`: `ssm.state_size = 128`, `ssm.time_step_rank = 48` (the v heads),\n    /// `ssm.conv_kernel = 4`, and `n_embd_r() = (d_conv-1) * (ssm_d_inner + 2*n_group*d_state) = 3 * 10240`.\n    int ssm_state_size = 128;\n    int ssm_v_heads = 48;\n    int ssm_d_conv = 4;\n    int ssm_conv_channels = 10240;\n\n    /// 36 of the 48 layers are GDN; the rest are QSA.  Declared as a derivation rather than a third constant,\n    /// because a `n_gdn_layers = 36` alongside `n_layers` and `n_qsa_layers` is a third thing to keep in step.\n    int n_gdn_layers() const { return n_layers - n_qsa_layers; }\n};\n\n// ---- byte costs ------------------------------------------------------------\nstruct Costs {\n    uint64_t expert_blob = 1382400; // one expert's gate_up+down, codes and scales (architecture §3.2)\n    uint64_t dense_bytes = 0;       // from the manifest: every non-expert tensor, canonical form\n    uint64_t embd_bytes = 0;        // token embedding\n    uint64_t mtp_bytes = 0;         // multi-token-prediction head, when present\n    uint64_t workspace_bytes = 0;\n    uint64_t state_bytes = 0; // GDN recurrence + conv history + replay log, per sequence\n};\n\n// GDN recurrence + conv history, bytes per sequence.  DERIVED, for the same reason everything else here is.\n//\n// This term was MISSING from the plan until round 198: `Costs::state_bytes` exists and `--state` exists, but\n// nothing passed it, so the planner was fed zero and quietly planned without it.  36 GDN layers of fp32 state\n// is **117.7 MB, or 85 expert cache slots** - not a rounding error.\n//\n//   recurrence    (S, h_v, S) fp32  = 128 * 48 * 128 * 4 = 3,145,728 B per layer\n//   conv history  (d_conv-1, C) fp32 =     3 * 10240 * 4 =   122,880 B per layer\n//\n// It is a FIXED cost and not a cache: it is state, it is resident for the life of a sequence, and it cannot be\n// evicted to make room for an expert.  A planner that omits it returns a plan it cannot honour, which is the\n// failure `DoesNotClose` exists to prevent.\ninline uint64_t state_bytes(const Geometry& g) {\n    const uint64_t per_layer = (uint64_t) g.ssm_state_size * (uint64_t) g.ssm_v_heads *\n                                   (uint64_t) g.ssm_state_size * sizeof(float) +\n                               (uint64_t) (g.ssm_d_conv - 1) * (uint64_t) g.ssm_conv_channels * sizeof(float);\n    return (uint64_t) g.n_gdn_layers() * per_layer;\n}\n\n// INT8 KV + indexer keys, bytes per token.  Both terms come from the geometry above and nothing else.\ninline uint64_t kv_bytes_per_token(const Geometry& g) {\n    const uint64_t kv_elems = 2ull * g.n_kv_heads * g.head_dim;       // K and V\n    const uint64_t kv_scales = (kv_elems / (uint64_t)g.kv_group) * 2; // fp16 scale per group\n    const uint64_t per_layer = kv_elems * 1 + kv_scales;              // INT8: one byte per element\n    // indexer: ONE cached key per block, `idx_dim` wide, SHARED across the query heads.  See the note on\n    // `indexer_key_heads` above - this term has been wrong in both directions and the derivation is why.\n    const uint64_t idx_layer =\n        (uint64_t) g.indexer_key_heads * (uint64_t) g.indexer_key_dim / (uint64_t) g.qsa_block;\n    return (uint64_t)g.n_qsa_layers * (per_layer + idx_layer);\n}\n\n// ---- the plan --------------------------------------------------------------\nstruct Plan {\n    uint64_t max_context = 0;\n    uint64_t kv_bytes = 0;    // KV + indexer keys at max_context\n    uint64_t state_bytes = 0; // GDN recurrence + conv history - FIXED, not evictable\n    uint64_t cache_bytes = 0; // what is left for expert cache slots\n    uint64_t cache_slots = 0;\n    uint64_t vram_budget = 0;\n    uint64_t vram_used = 0;\n    uint64_t dram_experts = 0; // the whole expert arena, streamed\n    std::vector<std::string> notes;\n};\n\n// Thrown when the requested context and the fixed costs cannot both fit.  A planner that returns a plan it\n// cannot honour is worse than one that fails, because the failure then happens at token 4000 instead of at\n// startup.\nstruct DoesNotClose : std::runtime_error {\n    explicit DoesNotClose(const std::string& w) : std::runtime_error(w) {}\n};\n\n// The VRAM budget that the KV cache and the expert cache share.  This is the one number taken from\n// `00-README.md` §2 rather than derived: the table's three rows all leave `KV + cache` constant, and that\n// constant is what the planner is dividing.  Expressed in bytes, decimal, matching how the table rounds.\ninline uint64_t vram_pool_bytes() {\n    return 5943000000ull;\n}\n\ninline Plan make_plan(uint64_t max_context, const Geometry& g, const Costs& c,\n                      uint64_t pool = vram_pool_bytes()) {\n    Plan p;\n    p.max_context = max_context;\n    p.vram_budget = pool;\n    p.kv_bytes = kv_bytes_per_token(g) * max_context;\n    p.state_bytes = c.state_bytes;\n    p.dram_experts = c.dense_bytes + c.embd_bytes; // costs that never enter the pool\n\n    const uint64_t fixed = c.dense_bytes + c.embd_bytes + c.mtp_bytes + c.workspace_bytes + c.state_bytes;\n    if (p.kv_bytes + fixed > pool) {\n        throw DoesNotClose(\"max-context \" + std::to_string(max_context) + \" needs \" +\n                           std::to_string(p.kv_bytes + fixed) + \" B of the \" + std::to_string(pool) +\n                           \" B VRAM pool; reduce --max-context\");\n    }\n    p.cache_bytes = pool - p.kv_bytes - fixed;\n    p.cache_slots = p.cache_bytes / c.expert_blob;\n    p.vram_used = pool - p.cache_bytes % c.expert_blob; // slot remainder is unusable, not free\n    if (p.cache_slots == 0) {\n        throw DoesNotClose(\"no room for even one expert cache slot at max-context \" +\n                           std::to_string(max_context));\n    }\n","stderr":""}

Hence the split API:\n//\n//     Ticket t = reader.issue(rows, n, out_raw);    // as soon as the token id is known\n//     ...                                           // embedding, layer 0\n//     reader.collect(t);                            // before layer 1 reads the rows\n//\n// `issue` also serves prefill: pass all 16 x N rows of a chunk; pages are deduplicated, sorted by offset and\n// kept at most `max_inflight` deep, so a chunk's reads can run while the previous chunk computes.\n//\n// THE ROW CACHE IS NOT THE TABLE. It keeps rows this process has already fetched (90 bytes each, bounded,\n// clock eviction). Measured on the frozen corpus (bench/results/2026-09-23-ngram-io): 1M rows (~95 MB)\n// would serve up to ~82% of reads; within one long prompt 20-34% of rows recur. Capacity 0 disables it.\n#pragma once\n\n#include \"strata/platform/direct_file.hpp\"\n\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <string>\n#include <vector>\n\nnamespace strata::ngram {\n\ninline constexpr uint32_t ROW_BYTES = 90;\ninline constexpr uint32_t PAGE = 4096;\n\nstruct ReaderStats {\n    uint64_t requests = 0;        ///< rows asked for\n    uint64_t cache_hits = 0;      ///< rows served from the row cache\n    uint64_t dedup_rows = 0;      ///< rows that shared a page already being read in the same ticket\n    uint64_t reads = 0;           ///< SSD read requests issued\n    uint64_t bytes = 0;           ///< bytes read from the SSD\n    double wait_us = 0;           ///< time `collect` spent blocked\n    double submit_us = 0;         ///< time spent inside the read submission call (non-zero = it blocks)\n    double read_us_sum = 0;       ///< sum of per-read latencies (issue to completion)\n    uint64_t late_injected = 0;   ///< reads delayed by fault injection\n    std::vector<float> read_us;   ///< last <= 65,536 read latencies, for percentiles\n    double percentile(double q) const;\n};\n\nclass PleReader {\npublic:\n    struct Ticket {\n        uint32_t id = 0;\n    };\n\n    PleReader();\n    ~PleReader();\n    PleReader(const PleReader&) = delete;\n    PleReader& operator=(const PleReader&) = delete;\n\n    /// `table_offset` is the byte offset of row 0 in the file and `n_rows` the row count; both come from a\n    /// validated GGUF parse (PleTable::open checks the table exactly fills the file from there).\n    /// `io_thread` (default): a worker thread submits and reaps reads, so `issue` costs the caller no ReadFile\n    /// calls. false: the caller's thread does it (A/B arm).\n    bool open(const std::string& path, uint64_t table_offset, uint64_t n_rows, uint32_t max_inflight,\n              uint64_t cache_rows, std::string& err, bool io_thread = true);\n    void close();\n    bool is_open() const;\n\n    /// Start fetching `n` rows; row i's 90 raw bytes land at `out_raw + 90 * i`. `out_raw` must stay valid\n    /// until `collect` returns. Out-of-range rows produce 90 zero bytes (the mmap path's behaviour).\n    Ticket issue(const uint32_t* rows, size_t n, uint8_t* out_raw);\n\n    /// Block until every row of the ticket is in `out_raw`. Returns false on an I/O error (message in `err`).\n    bool collect(Ticket t, std::string& err);\n\n    /// Fault injection for tests and for the plan's P2 exit check: every read completes no earlier than\n    /// `delay_us` after it was issued. 0 disables.\n    void set_injected_delay_us(double delay_us);\n\n    /// Read with no ticket in flight (the worker updates these while reads are outstanding).\n    const ReaderStats& stats() const;\n    void reset_stats();\n    uint64_t cache_capacity() const;\n    uint64_t cache_size() const;\n\nprivate:\n    struct Impl;\n    Impl* impl_ = nullptr;\n};\n\n}  // namespace strata::ngram\n=====\n86\n","stderr":""}

They were one number, which cannot distinguish a pool that is\n    // slow at the WORK from one that is slow at the SYNCHRONISATION - and those need opposite fixes.\n    const auto t_a = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();\n    while (parked_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != (uint32_t) n_) _mm_pause();\n    const auto t_b = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();\n    jobs_ = jobs;\n    njobs_ = n;\n    mode_ = 0;\n    head_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);\n    done_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);\n    epoch_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_release);   // release: jobs_/njobs_ are visible before the bump\n\n    // ---- **THE HOST DRAINS TOO (R2.2), INSTEAD OF SPINNING ON `done_`.**\n    //\n    // The loop below used to be `while (done_ != n) _mm_pause();`.  The host is pinned to core 0 - the core\n    // `physical_cores(true)` deliberately keeps the five workers off - so for the whole drain that core was\n    // idle while five cores did six cores' worth of work.  Measured before the change: 33.7 GB/s against\n    // 5/6 x 44.14 = 36.8 for five workers and 44.14 for six.\n    //\n    // The host claims through the SAME `head_` counter, so this is not a second scheduler and nothing about\n    // the ordering changes: `head_` is a single `fetch_add`, every job is the same size, and a thread that\n    // arrives late simply claims nothing.  `done_` is still the completion signal and the host still waits for\n    // it - what changed is only that the host arrives at that wait having done a share of the work.\n    //\n    // The host's `done_.fetch_add` is a release for the same reason a worker's is: `j.out` is read by the\n    // device after `run()` returns, so the write must be published, not merely performed.\n    if (host_works_) {\n        for (;;) {\n            const uint32_t i = head_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);\n            if (i >= (uint32_t) n) break;\n            const ExpertJob& j = jobs_[i];\n            s2_expert_vnni_q(j.blob, *j.act, j.out, host_scratch_);\n            done_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_release);\n        }\n    }\n\n    while (done_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != (uint32_t) n) _mm_pause();\n    // And park again, so the next `run` starts from a known state.  See the header for why `done` alone is\n    // not enough.\n    const auto t_c = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();\n    while (parked_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != (uint32_t) n_) _mm_pause();\n    const auto t_d = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();\n\n    ms_wait_park_ += std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t_b - t_a).count();\n    ms_drain_ += std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t_c - t_b).count();\n    ms_repark_ += std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t_d - t_c).count();\n}\n\n}  // namespace strata::kernels::cpu\n","stderr":""}

Measured 0.2800 ms per GDN block - 10 ms of a 71.5 ms\n/// token, 14%, in a kernel touching 12.6 MB that a 643 GB/s card should do in 0.020 ms.\n///\n/// The arithmetic does not change at all: the same columns are computed by the same code, in different blocks.\nconstexpr int MAX_H = 1;       ///< heads staged in shared memory per block\n\n/// ggml_compute_softplus_f32: log1p(exp(x)), with the large-x branch that avoids overflow.\n__device__ __forceinline__ float softplus_f(float x) { return x > 20.0f ? x : log1pf(expf(x)); }\n__device__ __forceinline__ float sigmoid_f(float x) { return 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-x)); }\n\n/// One step of the recurrence. {"returncode":0,"stdout":"=== src/kernels/cuda/s2_gemv_q8.cu (96 lines) ===\n// src/kernels/cuda/s2_gemv_q8.cu - the S2 GEMV that consumes Q8_0 ACTIVATIONS, as ggml does.\n//\n// THE GAP THIS CLOSES (round 186).  `ggml_mul_mat` converts src1 - the ACTIVATION - to the weight's\n// `vec_dot_type` before the dot product, and for Q2_0 that is Q8_0.  The CUDA kernels built in rounds 166-177\n// take FP16 activations instead, while the CPU expert path (`bench/micro/cpu_s2.cpp`) already quantizes to int8\n// and uses `vpdpbusd`.  Left that way the two paths compute different numbers for different experts of the SAME\n// token, and the measured size of the difference is the activation contract itself: 0.9498% relative, against\n// P2.S2's 1e-3 tolerance for FP16 paths.\n//\n// This is the CORRECTNESS version, not the fast one. The engine consumes token ids and produces text deltas; this module\n\n  * normalizes OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages requests into the chat template's message form,\n  * renders the model's own Jinja chat template (pack `tokenizer/chat_template.jinja`) exactly as Hugging Face\n    does (checked against the pack's `chat_golden.json`, 10 cases incl. thinking and tools),\n  * parses the streamed output incrementally into reasoning (`<think>...</think>`), content and tool calls in\n    the template's XML form (`<tool_call><function=NAME><parameter=P>VALUE</parameter>...</function></tool_call>`),\n    never emitting a partial tag to the client.\n\nDesign note: plan v0.3 describes a single C++ process. ## MODULE: verify_window_kernels (speculative verify: multi-token GDN, commit, helpers)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$T_{\max} = 8$$

**GDN conv+L2 multi:** For $t = 0 \ldots T-1$, conv over $[\text{history}(3) \mid \text{qkv}_0 \ldots \text{qkv}_t] \to \text{SiLU} \to \text{L2 norm}(q,k) \to h[t]$. History is NOT written. Bitwise equivalent to single-token kernel per token.

**GDN conv commit:** $\text{history} \leftarrow \text{last 3 of } [\text{history} \mid \text{qkv}_0 \ldots \text{qkv}_{n-1}]$, $n = *n_\text{keep}$ (device). $n=0$ leaves history unchanged.

**GDN step+norm multi:** Recurrence for $T$ tokens. With $n_\text{keep} = \text{null}$: state is read but NOT written (verify mode). With $n_\text{keep} \neq \text{null}$: first $*n_\text{keep}$ tokens replayed, state written (commit mode).

**wait\_flag\_ge:** Device spin until $*\text{flag} \ge \text{value}$ (mapped host flag). Value fixed at capture; supports multiple outstanding rings.

**fetch\_blobs:** Copy $*n$ blobs of $b$ bytes from mapped host memory into device VRAM with coalesced 16-byte loads — PCIe staging of missed experts before grouped kernel.

**embedding\_gather\_dev:** Embedding rows for $T$ token ids read from DEVICE memory (capturable).

## MODULE: expert_source_adapter (file-backed expert arena + VRAM cache bridge)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**FileExpertSource:** Memory-maps `experts.bin` ($N_L \times N_E \times 1{,}382{,}400$ bytes).

$$\text{blob}(l, e) = \text{base} + (l \cdot N_E + e) \cdot \text{BLOB}$$

**Critical:** NO `FILE_FLAG_RANDOM_ACCESS` on Windows — it disables read-ahead AND lets cache manager drop pages quickly. Measured 1.93 GB/s (disk speed) vs 44.14 GB/s (DRAM). The access IS random but every byte is re-read next token, so retention matters.

**ExpertSource adapter:** Bridges the host loop's `PoolFn`/`HitFn` callbacks to the `ExpertCache` and `FileExpertSource`. Handles:
- Hit/miss classification from the residency table
- Activation quantization (Q8_0 + fp32 scales for GPU parity)
- CPU pool dispatch for misses
- GPU grouped kernel launch for hits
- The two-phase protocol (Launch = GPU hits start; Combine = `parts += hit_out`)

## MODULE: layout_checks (per-layer tensor shape validation)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

For each layer $l \in [0, 48)$, validates every tensor's shape against `ModelGeometry`:
- 2-D tensors: `ne0` (contiguous axis) and `ne1` match kernel expectations
- 1-D tensors: element count AND `WeightKind` match

**Critical:** `WeightKind` matters. A BF16 1-D tensor occupies $2n$ bytes in the arena. Reading it as `const float*` reads $2n$ bytes = $n$ garbage floats. `ffn_gate_inp_shexp.weight` (BF16) read as f32 produced non-finite outputs in every MoE layer.

The indexer shape trap: `q_proj` = $[N_E, 4 \times 128]$ (4 QUERY heads), `k_proj` = $[N_E, 128]$ (1 KEY head). Confusing the two made the planner's indexer term 4× too big.

## MODULE: cpu_expert_pool (multi-threaded CPU expert dispatch)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**Physical core discovery:** Queries OS for physical cores (not logical/SMT siblings). Pinning one worker per physical core avoids halving bandwidth.

**Pool protocol:** Workers park on an atomic epoch counter. Run cycle:
1. Wait for all workers parked
2. Publish jobs + increment epoch (release fence)
3. Workers + host drain via `head_.fetch_add` (work-stealing)
4. Wait for `done_ == n_jobs`
5. Wait for re-park

**Host drains too (R2.2):** The host thread claims jobs through the SAME `head_` counter. Measured: 33.7 GB/s → 44.14 GB/s (5 workers → 6, using the previously idle pinned core 0).

**Split mode:** Two-phase (gate/up rows, then requantize, then down rows). Tasks = 3× threads per phase, partitioned across all experts' rows for tail-shortening.

**Multi-token mode:** Up to MAXT=8 tokens routed to the same expert. Blob read once for all tokens.

## MODULE: elementwise_kernels (embedding gather, SiLU, format conversion, add)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**embedding\_gather:** Column dequant. Code at bit position $(i \bmod \text{per\_byte}) \times \text{code\_bits}$. Value = $(c + c_\text{bias}) \times s[g] + o[g]$.

**gdn\_gate:** $\text{gate}_i = \text{softplus}(\alpha_i + dt_h) \times \text{ssm\_a}_h$, where $\text{softplus}(x) = \log(1 + e^x)$ with $x > 20 \Rightarrow x$ branch.

**silu:** Computed in DOUBLE then cast to f32, matching `ref/gdn.py`'s numpy: `np.exp` on f32 uses different algorithm than `expf`.

**add\_inplace:** $\text{dst}[i] \mathrel{+}= \text{src}[i]$. Lets R4's GPU half and CPU half write to the same `parts` buffer.

**to\_bf16 / to\_f16:** Format conversion kernels with proper rounding.

## MODULE: gdn_cuda (CUDA GDN recurrence kernel)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

One thread per $(h, j)$ column. State layout $(S, h_v, S)$, $j$ fastest.

**Block geometry:** `MAX_H = 1` (one head per block) → 192 blocks × 32 threads → 4 warps per SM. Previous `MAX_H = 8` had only 24 blocks (1 warp on 24 of 48 SMs). Kernel is latency-bound (strided global loads, ~600 cycle latency). Measured 0.2800 ms → much less with proper occupancy.

$q$, $k$ staged in shared memory per block (warp broadcast). Decay BEFORE update (Property 5).

**native\_gdn.cu:** Adapted from llama.cpp. Each warp owns one (head, column), retains 4 state rows in registers. Applies $\text{decay} = g \cdot s + k \cdot \delta$ formulation (decay folded into update). Scale = $1/\sqrt{S}$ applied to output.

## MODULE: kv_q8_kernels (INT8 KV cache append and gather)

**kv\_append\_q8:** Per 64-value group: $\text{amax} = \max_t |x_t|$, scale $= \text{f16}(\text{amax}/127)$, $q_t = \text{round}(x_t / \text{f32}(\text{scale}))$ clamped to $[-127, 127]$.

Quantizes against the STORED scale (fp16-rounded), not the exact scale. Two warps combine max through shared memory in fixed order.

Page table lookup: $\text{page} = \text{table}[\text{pos} / \text{page\_size}]$, row = page × heads × page\_size + head × page\_size + pos % page\_size.

**kv\_gather\_q8:** One thread = 4 consecutive values. Dequantizes: $x = q \times \text{f32}(\text{scale})$, output as fp16.

## MODULE: ple_cuda (PLE block GPU implementation)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Implements the PLE block from `include/strata/kernels/ple.hpp`:
1. key = grouped\_norm(ple\_key @ emb)
2. query = grouped\_norm(hidden, ple\_norm\_query)
3. value = ple\_value @ emb
4. gate = sigmoid(signed\_sqrt(dot(key, query) / sqrt(n\_embd)))
5. gated = value × gate (broadcast over hc streams)
6. normalized = grouped\_norm(gated, ple\_norm\_conv) ← **THIS is the conv input**
7. conv = sum\_k kW[k] × padded[hist + t − (kern−1−k)×dil]
8. out = hidden + gated + silu(conv)

**rms\_norm accumulation:** `(double)(x*x)` with product rounded in f32 first — matching ggml's `(ggml_float)(x[i00]*x[i00])`.

**history\_advance:** `hist[r, c] = hist[r+1, c]` then append normalized at row NG\_HIST−1. Row-fastest layout.

**Overlap check:** Scratch/output overlap rejected before any kernel launch.

## MODULE: qsa_block_select (QSA indexer block scoring and radix top-k)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**block\_scores:** For each block $b$ of $R=4$ tokens, score = $\sum_h \max(0, \langle k_b, q_h \rangle)$ (ReLU'd per-head dot products). The dead slot's key scores the partial block. Score kernel: 8 warps per block, float4 vectorized loads, warp-level reduction.

**block\_topk:** Radix-based top-k selection. 256-bin histogram per digit, most-significant digit first. Scans histogram to find the digit that contains the k-th element. O(B × digits) instead of O(B log B) sort.

## MODULE: router_top10 (MoE router softmax + top-k + renormalize)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$p = \text{softmax}(\text{logits}) \quad \text{(over ALL 512 experts)}$$
$$\text{ids} = \text{stable\_argsort}(-p)[:k] \quad \text{(ties by ascending index)}$$
$$w = \text{gather}(p, \text{ids})$$
$$s = \max(\sum w,\; 2^{-14})$$
$$\text{return ids},\; w / s$$

**Selection by rank** (not k repeated maxima):
$$\text{rank}(e) = |\{f : p[f] > p[e]\}| + |\{f < e : p[f] = p[e]\}|$$

This is stable descending argsort by ascending index, computed in ONE parallel pass.

**Why parallelized:** Original single-thread version: 3.39 ms/layer × 48 = 163 ms of 289 ms token (56% of forward pass).

**Double sum:** Still accumulated on ONE thread in ASCENDING order to keep last-bit agreement with reference.

**512 exponentials:** Computed ONCE each in parallel (old kernel: 11× redundant computation).

## MODULE: s2_gemv_q8_cuda (GPU S2 GEMV consuming Q8\_0 activations)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

For output row $o$:
$$y[o] = \sum_{q=0}^{n_\text{in}/4 - 1} \sum_{j=0}^{3} w_{o,4q+j} \cdot (x_q[j] \cdot d_x)$$

Where $w$ = Q2\_0 code dequantized: $(c - 1) \times d_w$, and activation $x$ = Q8\_0 block: int8 codes with fp16 scale $d_x$.

**Correctness version** (not speed-optimized): dequantizes each activation inside the loop. The dp4a optimization belongs to Phase 3. Partial sums in shared memory with tree reduction.

## MODULE: sampler_chain (penalties → top-k → top-p → temperature → pick)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**Order is critical** (transcribed from llama.cpp `common/sampling.cpp`):
1. **Penalties** (repeat/freq/presence): $\text{logit} \mathrel{*}= r$ if $\leq 0$, $\text{logit} \mathrel{/}= r$ if $> 0$; $-\text{count} \times f_\text{freq} - \mathbb{1}[\text{count}>0] \times f_\text{present}$
2. **Top-k:** 20 passes of maximum scan over 248,320 vocab
3. **Top-p:** Cumulative probability threshold
4. **Temperature:** Scale logits
5. **Pick:** Philox 4×32-10 CBRNG for reproducibility

**Greedy argmax** is a SEPARATE kernel (one block covering vocab) because the sampler's `<<<1, 64>>>` launch had 63 idle threads and ONE thread walking 248K logits. Measured 3.11 ms/token.

**Philox 4×32-10:** Counter-based RNG. Stream = f(seed, position), not f(previous draws). Batch can be sampled in any order; runs are reproducible.

## MODULE: ngram_host (n-gram hash and PLE table implementation)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Host-side implementation of the hash and table gather from `ngram.hpp`.

**Artifact constants:** Hardcoded from `docs/gguf-dump-shard1.txt`. Head vocab sizes are NOT arithmetic: 20000003, 20000023, 20000033, 20000047, ... (differences: 20, 10, 14, 12, 4, 6, 8, 4, 12, 14, 40, 6, 6, 2, 10).

**EOS propagation:** Predecessor scan evaluated BEFORE storing context. Position whose predecessor was EOS becomes EOS itself.

**PleTable::open (Direct mode):** Uses `PleReader` for unbuffered SSD reads. Drops any existing mmap. Row cache bounded at `cache_rows × 90` bytes.

**PleTable::gather (Mmap mode):** `PrefetchVirtualMemory` (Windows) issues all 16 row pages in one call. A/B arm: `--no-ple-prefetch` disables it.

## MODULE: suffix_drafter (speculative decoding draft proposals from suffix matching)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Hash table over 3-gram suffixes of the generated history. Key = mix-hash of last 3 tokens (splitmix64-style). Power-of-2 table, load factor ≤ 0.5, linear probing.

Each slot stores the N-most-recent positions (N = WAYS, typically 4). On lookup, extends the best match forward:

$$\text{proposal}[i] = \text{hist}[\text{best\_end} + 1 + i], \quad i = 0 \ldots \min(\text{max\_k}, \text{available}) - 1$$

**min\_match** (default 3) prevents very short, low-confidence matches.

## MODULE: mtp_pack_tool (MTP draft block GGUF packing)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Packs the 31 `mtp.*` tensors into a Strata GGUF for the multi-token prediction draft head.

**Q2\_0 quantization** (for expert weights): $d = \arg\min_{d'} \sum_i (x_i - (q_i - 1) \cdot d')^2$ over the 64-element block, grid $\{-1, 0, 1, 2\}$. The scale is chosen to MINIMIZE squared error (ggml reference sets $d = \max|w|$ and never uses the +2 level).

Dense tensors stay BF16/F32. Expert layout: `gate_up_proj` $[512, 1280, 2560]$ and `down_proj` $[512, 2560, 640]$.

## MODULE: memory_planner (VRAM budget arithmetic)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**Geometry** (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): $N_L = 48$, $N_\text{QSA} = 12$, $N_\text{GDN} = 36$, $n_{kv} = 2$, $d_h = 256$, $\text{kv\_group} = 64$, $\text{qsa\_block} = 4$.

**KV bytes per token:**
$$b_\text{KV/tok} = N_\text{QSA} \times \left( 2 \cdot n_{kv} \cdot d_h + \frac{2 \cdot n_{kv} \cdot d_h}{\text{kv\_group}} \cdot 2 + \frac{1 \cdot 128}{4} \right)$$

Indexer term: ONE cached key per block, 128-wide, shared across query heads. Round 194 had this 4× too big.

**GDN state bytes (FIXED, not evictable):**
$$b_\text{state} = 36 \times (128 \times 48 \times 128 \times 4 + 3 \times 10240 \times 4) = 117.7 \text{ MB}$$

This was MISSING until round 198 (85 expert cache slots lost).

**Plan:**
$$b_\text{cache} = b_\text{pool} - b_\text{KV} - b_\text{dense} - b_\text{embd} - b_\text{mtp} - b_\text{workspace} - b_\text{state}$$
$$\text{slots} = \lfloor b_\text{cache} / 1{,}382{,}400 \rfloor$$

VRAM pool = 5,943,000,000 bytes. `DoesNotClose` thrown if the plan cannot fit.

## MODULE: ple_ssd_reader (unbuffered SSD reader for the n-gram table)

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Table: 320,001,536 rows × 90 bytes = 26.8 GiB, NEVER held in RAM.

**Split API:**
$$\text{issue}(\text{rows}, n) \to \text{Ticket}$$
$$\text{collect}(\text{Ticket}) \to \text{ok}$$

Pages deduplicated and sorted by offset. Maximum `max_inflight` outstanding reads. IO thread submits reads asynchronously.

**Row cache:** Bounded clock-eviction cache. 1M rows × 90 B ≈ 95 MB serves ~82% of reads; within one long prompt 20–34% of rows recur.

**Latency hiding:** Issue as soon as token id is known; collect before layer 1 needs the rows.

# Strata Chunk 2/3 — Formal Theory

Reference: `Niko1221/Strata` commit `01529aaa82b9`

## MODULE: expert_dispatch (expert source + pool adapter)

**File scope:** `include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp` (355 lines).  The adapter between the session loop and the CPU/GPU expert evaluation.  Defines the `ExpertSource` interface, its two implementations (`FileExpertSource` — mmap, `ArenaExpertSource` — heap-copied pinned arena), the `ExpertDispatch` state machine, the `GpuPlanSink` for the verify window's GPU plan, and the free functions `expert_pool_dispatch`, `expert_pool_dispatch_multi`, `expert_hit_run`.

### ExpertSource (virtual interface)

$$
\textbf{ExpertSource} : \text{abstract interface for retrieving one expert blob}
$$

$$
\text{blob} : \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z} \to \{\texttt{uint8\_t}^{B} \cup \bot\}, \quad B = \text{BLOB} = 1{,}382{,}400
$$

$$
\text{Precondition: } 0 \le \text{layer} < N_L,\; 0 \le \text{expert} < N_E = 512

### FileExpertSource (mmap source, h = 0)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
\text{FileExpertSource} : \text{ExpertSource with } h = 0 \text{ (no caching, memory-mapped)}
$$

$$
\text{open}(\text{dir}, N_L, N_E) \to \{\top, \bot\} \quad \text{maps } \texttt{experts.bin}
$$

$$
\text{Precondition: } |\texttt{experts.bin}| = N_L \cdot N_E \cdot B, \quad B = 1{,}382{,}400
$$

$$
\text{blob}(l, e) = \text{base} + (l \cdot N_E + e) \cdot B
$$

$$
\text{Invariant: } \text{base} \ne \bot \implies \text{blobs} = N_L \cdot N_E
$$

$$
\textbf{Note: the OS page cache is the "cache".} \; \text{34 GB file + 26.8 GB n-gram shard} = 60.8\text{ GB on 63 GB machine}
$$
$$
\Rightarrow \text{page eviction under memory pressure} \Rightarrow \text{19 GB/s (engine) vs 42.8 GB/s (micro)}
$$

### GpuPlanSink

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
\text{GpuPlanSink}: \text{per-layer GPU plan for verify windows (VRAM hits + PCIe share of misses)}
$$

$$
\text{counts}[0] = N_{\text{groups}},\quad \text{counts}[1] = N_{\text{entries}},\quad \text{counts}[2] = N_{\text{PCIe groups}}
$$

$$
\forall g \in [0, N_{\text{groups}}): \;\text{entries in group } g = [\text{start}[g],\; \text{start}[g+1])
$$

$$
\forall i \in [0, N_{\text{entries}}): \text{dst}[i] = \text{token} \times k + j,\quad \text{tok}[i] = \text{token index}
$$

$$
\text{ptr}[g] : \text{device address of group } g\text{'s blob (VRAM slot)}
$$

$$
\text{ptr2}[q] : \text{PCIe staging slot } q \quad (\text{pcie\_mode} \in \{0:\text{DMA}, 1:\text{mapped arena}, 2:\text{copy kernel}\})
$$

$$
\text{publish}(\text{ctx}): \text{signals the GPU that the plan for this layer is in place}
$$

$$
\text{fetch}(\text{ctx}, \text{src}, n, \text{bytes}): \text{DMA } n \text{ host blobs into staging}
$$

### ExpertDispatch (the adapter state machine)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
\text{ExpertDispatch}: \text{per-session, reused every layer, zero allocation in token path}
$$

$$
\text{Invariants:}
$$
$$
\text{failed} \implies \forall l' > \text{fail\_layer}: \text{output is built on a hole (no recovery)}
$$
$$
\text{decided} \iff \text{is\_hit}[\cdot] \text{ was filled for this layer's ids}
$$
$$
\text{hit\_pending} \iff \text{Launch was called and Combine not yet called}
$$
$$
\text{hits\_ready}() = (\text{cache} \ne \bot) \wedge (\text{cache\_base} \ne \bot) \wedge (\text{parts\_out} \ne \bot) \wedge (\text{hit\_out} \ne \bot) \wedge (\text{mixed} \ne \bot) \wedge \ldots
$$

$$
\textbf{The split decision:} \quad \text{is\_hit}[j] = \begin{cases} 1 & (l, \text{ids}[j]) \text{ resident in VRAM cache} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise (CPU computes)} \end{cases}
$$

$$
\textbf{Latching failure:} \quad \text{failed} \gets \top \implies \text{never cleared during session}
$$

## MODULE: mtp_drafter (multi-token prediction draft layer)

**File scope:** `include/strata/core/mtp.hpp` (136 lines) + `src/core/mtp.cpp` (588 lines).  One MTP draft layer on the GPU: loads quantized dense weights and 512 expert blobs into VRAM, runs one transformer layer (embedding + hyper-connected attention + MoE) as captured CUDA graphs, produces T−1 draft tokens from the main model's final residual.

---

### MtpDrafter::load

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
\text{load}(\text{rt\_dir}, g, \text{ss}, \text{max\_t}) \to \{\top, \bot\}
$$

$$
\text{Reads: } \texttt{dense.txt} \text{ (index)},\; \texttt{dense.bin} \text{ (weights)},\; \texttt{experts.bin} \;(N_E \times B \text{ bytes})
$$

$$
\text{Allocates: } \text{dense weights on GPU},\; 512 \times 1{,}382{,}400 = 708\text{ MB experts on GPU}
$$

$$
\text{Allocates: } K/V\text{ state for the layer's own dense attention},\; \text{all intermediate buffers via bump allocator}
$$

$$
\text{Postcondition: } \text{max\_t} \in [1, \text{kVerifyMaxT}=8],\; \text{all required tensors present in dense.bin}
$$

$$
\text{VRAM} \approx 0.9\text{ GB total (experts + dense + buffers + K/V)}
$$

### MtpDrafter::record_forward

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
\text{record\_forward}(T, \text{step\_row0}, \text{cs}) \to \{\top, \bot\}
$$

$$
\textbf{Two branches (input):}
$$
$$
e = \text{fc\_embedding}(\text{RMSNorm}(\text{embed}(\text{tok})) \cdot (1+w))
$$
$$
h_c = \text{fc\_hidden}(\text{RMSNorm}_{10240}(R)) \cdot (1+w) \quad \forall c \in [0, hc)
$$
$$
R \gets h + e \quad \text{(broadcast } e \text{ across } hc \text{ streams)}
$$

$$
\textbf{Attention hyper-connection:} \quad \text{mixed}, \text{inject} = \text{gr\_read}(R, w_{\text{attn\_hc}})
$$

$$
\textbf{Dense QSA attention:} \quad K/V \text{ appended},\; Q \text{ projected and RoPE'd},\;
$$
$$
\text{attn} = \text{QSA\_decode\_batch}(Q, K, V) \to O\text{-proj} \to \text{bo}
$$

$$
\textbf{MLP hyper-connection:} \quad R \mathrel{+}= \text{gr\_write}(\text{bo}, \text{inject}),\; \text{mixed}' = \text{gr\_read}(R, w_{\text{mlp\_hc}})
$$

$$
\textbf{MoE:} \quad \text{logits} = \text{mixed}' \cdot w_{\text{gate}}^T,\; (\text{ids}, w) = \text{top-}10(\text{logits})
$$
$$
\text{parts} = \text{grouped\_S2}(\text{ids}, \text{mixed}'),\; y = \sum_j w_j \cdot \text{parts}_j + \text{shared\_expert}(\text{mixed}')
$$
$$
R \mathrel{+}= \text{gr\_write}(y, \text{inject}_{\text{mlp}})
$$

$$
\textbf{Final mixer + head:} \quad \text{sample} = \text{gr\_read}(R, w_{\text{mixer}}, \text{no inject})
$$
$$
\text{token} = \arg\max(\text{head}(\text{sample}))
$$

$$
\text{When step\_row0} < 0: \text{K/V-only mode (prefill), no full layer}
$$

```lean
-- axle_verify: formal_statement / content

    (T : Nat) (full : Bool) (h_full : full = true) (h_T : T = 1 ∨ full = false) :
    full = true → T = 1 := by sorry

-- proof
theorem mtp_full_layer_single_token
    (T : Nat) (full : Bool) (h_full : full = true) (h_T : T = 1 ∨ full = false) :
    full = true → T = 1 := by
  intro hf
  cases h_T with
  | inl h => exact h
  | inr h => rw [hf] at h; exact absurd h Bool.noConfusion
```

```cpp
    const bool full = argrow0 >= 0;
    const int row0 = full ? argrow0 : -1 - argrow0;
    if (full && argcount != 1) { err = "..."; return false; }
    // ---- two input branches: embed + fc_embedding, Rin + fc_hidden

    // ---- QSA attention: K/V append, Q project, RoPE, decode_attn_batch, gate, O-proj
    // ---- MLP hyper-connection: fused_gr_read_multi with bo_prev
```

## MODULE: verify_window (speculative verify)

**File scope:** `include/strata/core/verify.hpp` (161 lines).  T tokens (last accepted + T−1 drafts) go through all 48 layers in ONE captured graph.  Per-token argmax is bit-for-bit greedy decode.  `commit(n_keep)` advances GDN conv history, restores indexer tail, sets PLE history.

---

### Verifier

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
\text{Verifier}: \text{T tokens at positions } [p_0, p_0+T) \text{ through 48 layers in one captured graph}
$$

$$
\text{init}(wt, g, ss, \text{hits}, \text{head}, \text{max\_t}) \to \{\top, \bot\}
$$

$$
\text{run}(T, \text{tokens}, p_0, \text{pool}, \text{user}, \text{out}) \to \{\top, \bot\}
$$

$$
\text{Postcondition: } \text{out}[t] = \arg\max_v P(v | \text{tokens}[0..t]) \quad \text{bit-for-bit = greedy decode}
$$

$$
\textbf{State mutation:} \quad K/V\text{ appended for all } T \text{ positions; GDN state UNTOUCHED}
$$

$$
\text{commit}(n_{\text{keep}}) : \text{make first } n_{\text{keep}} \text{ tokens permanent}
$$

$$
\text{GDN conv history replayed from stored inputs for } [0, n_{\text{keep}})
$$

$$
\text{Indexer tail restored from snapshot, accepted keys re-appended}
$$

$$
\text{PLE history set to snapshot after token } n_{\text{keep}}-1
$$

$$
\textbf{Expert cost:} \quad \text{CPU misses} \approx 1.75\times \text{(T=2)},\; 2.4\times \text{(T=3)},\; 3.05\times \text{(T=4)} \;\text{of single token}
$$

$$
\text{PoolMultiFn}: (x_f^{(T \times N)}, \text{ids}^{(T \times k)}) \to \text{out}^{(Tk \times N)}, \;\text{hit rows zeroed}
$$

## MODULE: cpu_expert_pool (CPU thread pool for expert evaluation)

**File scope:** `include/strata/kernels/cpu/pool.hpp` (196 lines).  A flat-batch thread pool for running K expert evaluations per layer on physical CPU cores, with fetch_add claim, done/parked completion protocol, and cache-line-isolated atomics.

\textbf{Completion protocol:}
$$
$$
\text{run}(J, n): \text{publish } n \text{ jobs, block until } \text{done} = n \text{ AND every worker PARKED}
$$

$$
\textbf{Why done alone is insufficient:} \text{a worker can be inside the drain loop after its last done++}
$$
$$
\text{If host resets head, that worker claims a job from the NEXT batch before it's published}
$$

$$
\textbf{Cache-line isolation (review finding C3):}
$$
$$
\text{head\_, done\_, parked\_, epoch\_, stop\_} : \text{each } \texttt{alignas(64)} \text{ to prevent false sharing}
$$

$$
\text{host\_works}: \text{the host thread joins the drain (6th core, measured 33.7 → 36.8 GB/s potential)}
$$

$$
\text{run\_split}(J, n): \text{each expert split by rows across all threads (gate/up, then quantize, then down)}
$$

$$
\text{run\_split\_multi}: \text{multi-token, each expert's rows read once for all its tokens}
$$

## MODULE: gated_residual (hyper-connection read/write)

**File scope:** `include/strata/kernels/gr.hpp` (123 lines).  The gated residual (hyper-connection) from qwen4exp: `gr_read` collapses an `hc`-stream residual stack to the vector the mixer consumes + per-stream injection; `gr_write` puts the mixer's output back into every stream.

---

### gr_read

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
\text{gr\_read}: R \in \mathbb{R}^{hc \times N} \to (\text{mixed} \in \mathbb{R}^N, \text{inject} \in \mathbb{R}^{hc})
$$

$$
x_n[c,i] = \text{RMSNorm}(R[c], w_{\text{norm}}[c]) \quad \text{where } w_{\text{norm}} \text{ is stored as } (1+w)
$$

$$
\text{lo} = \text{SiLU}\!\left(\frac{x_q \cdot w_{\text{down}}^T}{hc}\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{hc_{lr}} \quad (\text{division INSIDE silu})
$$

$$
\text{gate}[c, i] = \sigma(\text{lo} \cdot w_{\text{up}}^T)[c, i]
$$

$$
\text{mixed}[i] = \frac{1}{hc}\sum_{c=0}^{hc-1} x_n[c,i] \cdot \text{gate}[c,i]
$$

$$
\text{inject}[c] = x_q \cdot w_{\text{inject}}^T \quad (\text{or untouched if } w_{\text{inject}} = \bot)
$$

$$
\textbf{Activation contract:} \quad x_q = \begin{cases} \text{bf16}(x_n) & \text{default} \\ x_n & \text{fp32 mode} \end{cases},\quad \text{lo}_q = \begin{cases} \text{bf16}(\text{lo}) & \text{default} \\ \text{lo} & \text{fp32} \end{cases}
$$

$$
\textbf{Weights:} \quad \text{BF16, stored as high 16 bits of f32 in uint16\_t} \;(\text{saves 1.374 GiB})
$$

### gr_write

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
\text{gr\_write}: (R, \text{block\_out}, \text{inject}) \to R_{\text{out}}
$$

$$
w[c] = 2 \cdot \sigma\!\left(\frac{\text{inject}[c]}{hc}\right) \quad \text{(centred on 1: zero injection = plain residual add)}
$$

$$
R_{\text{out}}[c, i] = R[c, i] + \text{block\_out}[i \bmod N] \cdot w[c]
$$

$$
\text{Note: block\_out is added to EVERY stream identically; only the weight is per-stream}
$$

## MODULE: ple_block (PLE n-gram block)

**File scope:** `include/strata/kernels/ple.hpp` (120 lines).  One PLE token: 16 gathered rows of 160 → a residual-stack update.  Grouped norm, signed-sqrt gate, 1D convolution over normalized history rows.

---

### ple_block

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
\text{ple\_block}(\text{emb}, \text{hidden}, \text{hist\_rows}, w) \to \text{result}
$$

$$
\text{key} = \text{GroupedNorm}(w_{\text{key}} \cdot \text{emb}, w_{\text{norm\_key}}) \in \mathbb{R}^{hc\_dim}
$$

$$
\text{query} = \text{GroupedNorm}(\text{hidden}, w_{\text{norm\_query}}) \in \mathbb{R}^{hc\_dim}
$$

$$
\text{value} = w_{\text{value}} \cdot \text{emb} \in \mathbb{R}^{N}
$$

$$
s[c] = \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} \sum_d \text{key}[c,d] \cdot \text{query}[c,d]
$$

$$
\text{gate}[c] = \sigma\!\left(\text{sign}(s[c]) \cdot \sqrt{\max(|s[c]|, 10^{-6})}\right) \quad \text{(signed square root)}
$$

$$
\text{gated}[c, d] = \text{value}[d] \cdot \text{gate}[c] \quad \text{(broadcast over hc streams)}
$$

$$
\text{normalized} = \text{GroupedNorm}(\text{gated}, w_{\text{norm\_conv}})
$$

$$
\text{conv}[c] = \sum_{k=0}^{3} w_{\text{conv1d}}[k, c] \cdot \text{padded}[\text{hist} + t - (3-k) \cdot \text{dil}][c]
$$

$$
\text{result} = \text{hidden} + \text{gated} + \text{SiLU}(\text{conv})
$$

$$
\textbf{Critical:} \text{ the conv input is } \texttt{normalized} \text{ (not gated values directly); ref/ngram.py docstring is wrong}
$$

$$
\textbf{History layout:} \text{ ROW-FASTEST: } \text{hist\_rows}[\text{row} + \text{NG\_HIST} \cdot \text{channel}]
$$

$$
\textbf{Conv weight layout:} \text{ GGML-native: flat index } k + 4 \cdot c \text{ (transposed from numpy)}
$$

## MODULE: s_family_gemv (S-form GEMV kernels)

**File scope:** `include/strata/kernels/s_gemv.hpp` (134 lines).  Unified GEMV for S2/S4/S8 canonical weight forms: one kernel family, three code widths, parameterized by codebook/bias/group/offset attributes.  Multiple variants: basic, row-split, Q8_K activation, Q8_0 activation.

---

### SForm + s_gemv

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
\text{SForm}: (\text{code\_bits} \in \{2,4,8\}, \text{code\_bias}, \text{group\_elems}, \text{codebook} \in \{\text{Affine}, \text{Iq4Nl}\}, \text{has\_offset}, \text{act\_kind})
$$

$$
\text{Canonical decode:} \quad \text{value} = cb[\text{code}] \cdot \text{scale} + \text{offset}
$$

$$
\text{where } cb[\text{code}] = \begin{cases} \text{code} + \text{bias} & \text{Affine} \\ \text{kvalues\_iq4nl}[\text{code}] & \text{Iq4Nl} \end{cases}
$$

$$
\text{s\_gemv}: y[o] = \sum_i \text{fp16}(x[i]) \cdot W[o, i] \quad \text{(GGUF layout: row } o \text{ is contiguous in } n_{\text{in}}\text{)}
$$

$$
\text{s\_gemv\_split}: \text{same, one block of } T_r \text{ threads per output row, strided reduction through shmem}
$$

$$
\textbf{NOT bit-identical to s\_gemv} \text{ (different partial-sum order → parity test carries tolerance)}
$$

$$
\text{act\_kind} \in \{0, 1\}: \quad 0 = \text{Q8\_0 activation},\; 1 = \text{Q8\_K activation}
$$

$$
\textbf{act\_kind is carried, not derived:} \text{ Q5\_0 and Q5\_K both 8-bit bias -16; IQ4\_NL and IQ4\_XS both Iq4Nl no offset}
$$

### s_gemv_q8k / s_gemv_q8k_split / s_gemv_q8_0_split

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
\text{s\_gemv\_q8k}: y[o] = \sum_i \text{dequant\_q8k}(x, i) \cdot W[o, i]
$$

$$
\text{block\_q8\_k layout}: 292 \text{ bytes per 256 elements: } \{d: \text{f32},\; qs: \text{int8}[256],\; bsums: \text{int16}[16]\}
$$

$$
\text{dequant: } x[i] = d \cdot qs[i] \quad (\text{one multiply per element, same cost as fp16 path})
$$

$$
\textbf{Weight decode is the SAME code as s\_gemv — one implementation of canonical form}
$$

$$
\text{s\_gemv\_q8k\_split}: \text{WARP per output row (fixed), no tunable threads\_per\_row}
$$

$$
\textbf{threads\_per\_row was removed from this signature because the impl threw it away}
$$

$$
\text{s\_gemv\_q8\_0\_split}: y[o] = \sum_i \text{dequant\_q8\_0}(x, i) \cdot W[o, i]
$$

$$
\text{block\_q8\_0}: 34 \text{ bytes per 32 elements: } \{d: \text{fp16},\; qs: \text{int8}[32]\}
$$

$$
\textbf{This kernel was missing:} \text{ legacy block formats (Q2\_0, IQ4\_NL, ...) use vec\_dot\_type Q8\_0, not Q8\_K}
$$

$$
n_{\text{in}} \text{ must be multiple of 32};\; \text{group\_elems power of 2 and multiple of 4}
$$

## MODULE: f16_conversions (IEEE 754 half-precision bit manipulation)

**File scope:** `include/strata/kernels/f16_bits.hpp` (97 lines).  Manual fp16↔fp32 conversions as bit manipulation, because `__float2half` produced wrong bits (0x2600 for 0x26DB, 0x3C01 for 1.0).  Round-to-nearest-even.

---

### f16_from_f32

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
\text{f16\_from\_f32}: \mathbb{R}_{\text{f32}} \to \text{uint16\_t (fp16 bits)}
$$

$$
\textbf{Rounding: round-to-nearest-even (IEEE 754 default)}
$$

$$
\textbf{Three regimes:}
$$
$$
\text{Normal: } 1 \le \text{exp} \le 30: \text{mantissa rounded from 13 surviving bits with sticky remainder}
$$
$$
\text{Subnormal: } \text{exp} \le 0: \text{implicit 1 restored, shift right, rounding point MOVES}
$$
$$
\text{Overflow: } \text{exp} \ge 31 \text{ (finite)} \to +\infty \;(0\text{x7C00});\quad \text{NaN input} \to \text{NaN}
$$

$$
\textbf{Bug fix (round 198):} \text{ finite overflow (1e30, 65536) → inf, NOT NaN}
$$
$$
\text{Earlier version conflated f32 inf/NaN (rawexp=255) with finite overflow}
$$

#### LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)

```lean

-- axle_verify: formal_statement / content

-- proof
theorem f16_inf_is_0x7c00 : (0x7C00 : Nat) = 31744 := by
  norm_num
```

```lean
  subst h; norm_num
```

#### LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE

```cpp
STRATA_HD inline uint16_t adj_from_f32(float f) {
    uint32_t x;
    std::memcpy(&x, &f, 4);
    const uint32_t sign = (x >> 16) & 0x8000u;
    const uint32_t rawexp = (x >> 23) & 0xFFu;
    int exp = (int) rawexp - 127 + 15;
    uint32_t man = x & 0x7FFFFFu;
    if (rawexp == 0xFFu) return (uint16_t) (sign | 0x7C00u | (man ? 0x200u : 0u));
    if (exp >= 31) return (uint16_t) (sign | 0x7C00u);
    if (exp <= 0) {
        if (exp < -10) return (uint16_t) sign;
        man |= 0x800000u;
        const uint32_t sh = (uint32_t) (14 - exp);
        uint32_t h = (man >> sh) & 0x3FFu;
        const uint32_t rem = man & ((1u << sh) - 1u);
        if (rem > (1u << (sh - 1)) || (rem == (1u << (sh - 1)) && (h & 1u))) ++h;
        return (uint16_t) (sign | h);
    }
    uint16_t h = (uint16_t) (sign | ((uint32_t) exp << 10) | (man >> 13));
    const uint32_t rem = man & 0x1FFFu;
    if (rem > 0x1000u || (rem == 0x1000u && (h & 1u))) ++h;
    return h;
}
```

### f32_from_f16

#### LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE

```cpp
STRATA_HD inline float adj_from_f16(uint16_t h) {
    const uint32_t sign = (uint32_t) (h & 0x8000u) << 16;
    const uint32_t ex = (h >> 10) & 0x1Fu, man = h & 0x3FFu;
    uint32_t argresult;
    if (ex == 0) {
        if (man == 0) {
            argresult = sign;
        } else {
            uint32_t m = man;
            int s = 0;
            while ((m & 0x400u) == 0) { m <<= 1; ++s; }
            argresult = sign | ((uint32_t) (113 - s) << 23) | ((m & 0x3FFu) << 13);
        }
    } else if (ex == 31) {
        argresult = sign | 0x7F800000u | (man << 13);
    } else {
        argresult = sign | ((ex - 15 + 127) << 23) | (man << 13);
    }
    float f;
    std::memcpy(&f, &argresult, 4);
    return f;
}
```

r.ne1 : 1);\n            wr.kind = r.kind;\n            wr.code_bits = r.code_bits;\n            wr.code_bias = r.code_bias;\n            wr.group_elems = r.group_elems;\n            wr.codebook_iq4nl = r.codebook != 0;\n            wr.has_offset = r.has_offset != 0;\n            wr.codes_bytes = r.codes_bytes;\n            wr.scales_bytes = r.scales_bytes;\n            wr.offset_bytes = r.offset_bytes;\n            wr.src_off = r.src_off;\n            wr.src_bytes = r.src_bytes;\n            wr.file_id = r.file;\n            wr.scales_fp16 = r.scales_fp16 != 0;\n            wr.act_kind = r.act_kind;\n            table_[r.name] = wr;\n            ++report_.tensors;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if (r.code_bits != 0 && r.dst_bytes == 0) {\n            // plan v0.3 P6: a native pack's row that carries a shape only - the GGUF form must serve it\n            err = r.name + \": this pack holds the tensor only in its GGUF form (run with --native SHARD1)\";\n            cudaFreeHost(stage_in); cudaFreeHost(stage_out);\n            return false;\n        }\n        if (r.file != cur_file) {\n            if (cur) std::fclose(cur);\n            const char* fn = file_name(r.file);\n            const std::string p = pack_dir + \"/\" + (fn ? The two promoted types shrink\n            // 4 B/elem to 2; the rest are already the engine form.\n            Conv c = Conv::Copy;\n            if (r.raw16) c = Conv::Copy;\n            else if (r.kind == WeightKind::Bf16InF32) c = Conv::Bf16High;\n            else if (r.kind == WeightKind::F16InF32) c = Conv::ToF16;\n            const uint64_t elems = (uint64_t) r.ne0 * (uint64_t) (r.ne1 > 0 ? r.ne1 : 1);\n            if (c != Conv::Copy && (r.src_bytes != elems * 4 || r.dst_bytes != elems * 2)) {\n                // A promoted type is 4 B/elem in and 2 B/elem out, and nothing else. It is checked against both recorded totals, not trusted.\n        if (!bad && (sum_src != r.src_bytes || sum_dst != r.dst_bytes)) {\n            char buf[360];\n            std::snprintf(buf, sizeof buf,\n                          \"%s: the segments cover %llu/%llu B but the index says %llu/%llu - the plane layout \"\n                          \"this loader built is not the one the index describes\",\n                          r.name.c_str(), (unsigned long long) sum_src, (unsigned long long) sum_dst,\n                          (unsigned long long) r.src_bytes, (unsigned long long) r.dst_bytes);\n            err = buf;\n            bad = true;\n        }\n        if (bad) { cudaFreeHost(stage_in); cudaFreeHost(stage_out); return false; }\n\n        for (int si = 0; si < n_segs; ++si) {\n            const Seg& s = segs[si];\n            const bool widening = (s.conv == Conv::WidenF16);\n            if (widening && (s.src_bytes & 1ull)) {\n                err = r.name + \": an fp16 plane with an odd source byte count\";\n                cudaFreeHost(stage_in); cudaFreeHost(stage_out);\n                return false;\n            }\n            uint64_t done = 0;\n            while (done < s.src_bytes) {\n                uint64_t n = std::min(CHUNK, s.src_bytes - done);\n                // WIDENING NEVER SPLITS AN ELEMENT.  CHUNK is even, so a full chunk cannot, but the tail of a\n                // plane whose length is odd would - and half an fp16 is a plausible-looking scale.\n                if (widening && (n & 1ull)) {\n                    if (n == 1) { err = r.name + \": an fp16 plane ending on a half element\"; cudaFreeHost(stage_in); cudaFreeHost(stage_out); return false; }\n                    n -= 1;\n                }\n                if (!read_at(cur, r.src_off + s.src_off + done, stage_in, (size_t) n, err, r.name.c_str())) {\n                    cudaFreeHost(stage_in); cudaFreeHost(stage_out);\n                    return false;\n                }\n                const uint8_t* src = (const uint8_t*) stage_in;\n                const void* host_src = src;\n                uint64_t out_bytes = n;\n                uint64_t out_at = s.dst_off + done;\n\n                switch (s.conv) {\n                    case Conv::Copy:\n                        break;\n                    case Conv::Bf16High: {\n                        // THE HIGH 16 BITS ARE THE BF16 ENCODING, exactly - not a rounding.
